issues.legal_issue: A statutory debt-recovery tribunal cannot grant a third party liberty to bring a separate action against a bank when that issue falls outside the tribunal’s limited statutory jurisdiction, particularly where the bank was not party to the compromise underlying the order.
material_facts: A borrower appealed a debt-recovery order, and the borrower and the auction purchaser reached a compromise that did not include the bank.
The appellate tribunal directed the bank to refund the auction purchaser’s deposit with interest and granted the purchaser liberty to bring an action against the bank for any omission.
The bank had not been found at fault, and it challenged the grant of liberty; the High Court declined to interfere.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal’s grant of liberty was beyond its jurisdiction. The Supreme Court deleted that observation and set aside the High Court’s refusal to interfere.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17 and 18 of the SARFAESI Act, the tribunals adjudicate matters within the statutory scheme, including the powers specified in Section 17(3); Section 19 provides for compensation and costs in specified circumstances. Section 19(25) of the RDB Act gives a tribunal limited power to make orders needed to give effect to its orders, prevent abuse of process, or secure the ends of justice, but does not confer inherent or general jurisdiction. Section 34 of the SARFAESI Act reinforces the tribunals’ defined statutory role. The Court relied on Upper Doab Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Shahdara (Delhi) Saharanpur Light Rly. Co. Ltd. and Union of India v. Orient Paper and Industries Ltd. for the principle that a tribunal cannot order relief for which it has not been given jurisdiction, and on Union of India v. R. Gandhi for the distinction between courts and statutory tribunals.

predicates.statutory_debt_recovery_tribunal_proceed: A tribunal established to decide debt-recovery disputes considered an appeal or application within that statutory scheme.
predicates.tribunal_granted_separate_action_liberty: The tribunal stated that a person could bring a separate action against another party.
predicates.proposed_defendant_not_party_to_compromi: The person against whom the separate action could be brought was not a party to the compromise on which the tribunal’s order was based.

issues.definition: When a debt-recovery tribunal grants liberty for a separate action against someone who was not party to the underlying compromise, the tribunal lacks authority to grant that liberty.

issues.legal_issue: Debt-recovery tribunals must decide matters promptly, and adjournments should be exceptional rather than routine.
material_facts: An appeal before the appellate tribunal was repeatedly adjourned and remained undecided for about four and a half years.
The appeal concerned measures taken in connection with recovery of a bank loan, and the delay impeded resolution of the dispute.
issues.conclusion: The appellate tribunal failed to meet its obligations by allowing prolonged delay and routine adjournments; tribunals dealing with these matters must act promptly and treat adjournments as exceptional.
issues.legal_principle: The SARFAESI Act and the RDB Act are intended to facilitate speedy adjudication and recovery. Section 17(5) of the SARFAESI Act prescribes a time for disposal of applications and provides for an outer limit, while Section 22 of the RDB Act permits tribunals to regulate their procedure, guided by natural justice. The Court relied on Mardia Chemicals Ltd. v. Union of India, Authorised Officer, Indian Overseas Bank v. Ashok Saw Mill, United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon, Transcore v. Union of India, and Official Liquidator, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand v. Allahabad Bank on the statutory purpose, the importance of time, and the tribunals’ role in expeditious adjudication.

predicates.debt_recovery_tribunal_proceeding: A debt-recovery tribunal or appellate tribunal is considering an application or appeal about recovery of a debt or enforcement of security.
predicates.repeated_adjournments: The tribunal repeatedly postponed consideration of the matter.
predicates.prolonged_undecided_period: The matter remained undecided for a substantial period.

issues.definition: When a debt-recovery tribunal repeatedly adjourns a matter and leaves it undecided for a substantial period, it must act promptly and treat further adjournments as exceptional.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal appeal need not be remitted for a fresh hearing when the party seeking remand did not challenge the tribunal order, the appeal before the Supreme Court was confined to a separate issue, and the recovery and transfer of the property had already occurred.
material_facts: The auction purchaser did not challenge the appellate tribunal’s order before the High Court or the Supreme Court.
The bank confined its challenge to the tribunal’s grant of liberty for a separate action against it.
By the time of the Supreme Court’s decision, the bank had realized its money and the property had changed hands.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to set aside the appellate tribunal’s order in its entirety or remit the appeal for a fresh hearing.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined remand in light of the limits of the challenge before it and the completed recovery and subsequent change in ownership. It relied on the procedural posture of the case rather than stating a separate statutory test for remand.

rule.if: debt_recovery_appeal and challenger_confined_to_separate_issue and auction_purchaser_did_not_challenge_order and recovery_completed and property_changed_hands

predicates.debt_recovery_appeal: A court is considering an appeal arising from a debt-recovery tribunal proceeding.
predicates.challenger_confined_to_separate_issue: The party seeking relief limited its challenge to a distinct part of the tribunal’s order.
predicates.auction_purchaser_did_not_challenge_orde: The auction purchaser did not challenge the tribunal’s order in the proceedings under review.
predicates.recovery_completed: The bank had received the money it was owed.
predicates.property_changed_hands: The property had been transferred after the tribunal’s order.

issues.definition: When a debt-recovery appeal is confined to a distinct issue, the auction purchaser did not challenge the order, and recovery and transfer of the property are complete, the court may decline a fresh hearing.
